title: How the U.S. Hid a Deadly Airstrike

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯Dealbook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市Dealbook峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界一些极具影响力的领袖，包括J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: November 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维尔尼西，《纽约时报》出品。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: A Times investigation reveals one of the largest civilian casualty events of the war against the
sentences.zh: 《时报》的一项调查揭露了打击伊斯兰国

sentences.en: Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 战争中规模最大的平民伤亡事件之一。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague, Dave Phillips, on how the system designed to bring this to light ended up keeping it hidden.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事戴夫·菲利普斯，探讨了旨在将此事公之于众的系统最终如何将其掩盖。

sentences.en: It's Monday, November 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月15日，星期一。

sentences.en: Dave, where does this story start?
sentences.zh: 戴夫，这个故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: This story starts March 18th, 2019, in a big Air Force combat operations center in Al-Yudid in
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于2019年3月18日，地点在卡塔尔乌代德的大型空军作战指挥中心。

sentences.en: Qatar.
sentences.zh: 卡塔尔。

sentences.en: And there we have, it almost looks like mission command for NASA.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里看到的情景，看起来几乎就像美国宇航局的任务指挥中心。

sentences.en: You have banks of computers, big screens, all of them watching the air war against the Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 这里有一排排的计算机、大屏幕，所有人都在监视针对伊斯兰国的空战。

sentences.en: The coalition had over years and thousands of airstrikes basically clawed away its territory once the group had controlled millions of acres.
sentences.zh: 多年来，联军通过数千次空袭，基本上夺回了该组织曾经控制数百万英亩的领土。

sentences.en: But by that day in March, they only controlled about one square mile of dirt fields pressed against the Euphrates River in Syria.
sentences.zh: 但到了3月的那个日子，他们只控制了叙利亚幼发拉底河畔约一平方英里的泥土地。

sentences.en: And on this day, a lot of people in the command center are watching a drone that was flying up overhead.
sentences.zh: 就在3月的这一天，指挥中心里的许多人都在盯着一架在头顶飞行的无人机。

sentences.en: Now, what they saw was a field that was just littered with a tangle of cars and makeshift tents, of debris, of the leftovers from weeks of combat.
sentences.zh: 当时，他们看到一片场地上散落着乱七八糟的汽车、临时帐篷、残骸，以及数周战斗留下的废墟。

sentences.en: But also within there was a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但在其中还有许多人。

sentences.en: And the drone hovered over and focused in on a group of women and children who had found refuge down by the river against a steep sandbank.
sentences.zh: 无人机盘旋着，将镜头对准了一群在河边陡峭沙堤下寻求庇护的妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: The drone, it lingered for several minutes, slowly circling with its cameras focused on these folks,
sentences.zh: 无人机盘旋了几分钟，缓慢盘旋着，镜头始终对准这些人，

sentences.en: either sleeping or just laying down low to take cover from whatever combat might be coming.
sentences.zh: 他们要么在睡觉，要么只是趴在地上，以此躲避可能降临的战火。

sentences.en: And the people in the operation center were calmly watching this when suddenly they saw something cross their screens that they didn't expect.
sentences.zh: 作战中心的人正平静地看着这一幕，突然，他们看到屏幕上闪过一个意想不到的画面。

sentences.en: An American F-15 attack jet came right through and dropped a large bomb dead center into this group of women and children.
sentences.zh: 一架美国F-15攻击机呼啸而过，向这群妇女和儿童的正中心投下了一枚大型炸弹。

sentences.en: And there was this shuddering blast that basically filled the whole view of the drone camera and engulfed all of these people, killing nearly all of them.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一声震撼的爆炸，几乎填满了无人机摄像头的整个视野，并将所有人吞没，几乎炸死了所有人。

sentences.en: So there's all these people in the operation center that don't know what the heck is going on, and they scramble to try and piece things together.
sentences.zh: 因此，作战中心里的所有人都不知到底发生了什么，他们手忙脚乱地试图拼凑出事情的真相。

sentences.en: There's chatting with each other over secure chat logs, just trying to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 他们在加密聊天日志中互相交流，拼命想要弄明白情况。

sentences.en: One of them immediately types out, who dropped that?
sentences.zh: 其中一人立即打字问道：是谁投的弹？

sentences.en: Meaning the bomb.
sentences.zh: 指的是炸弹。

sentences.en: And another one says, we just dropped on 50 women and children.
sentences.zh: 另一个人说：我们刚刚炸了50名妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: So what did those people in the room do?
sentences.zh: 那么房间里的那些人做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the first thing they did was they followed their training.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们做的第一件事就是遵循他们的训练。

sentences.en: They did what's called a battle damage assessment, basically a count of what got hit.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了所谓的战果评估，也就是对被炸毁的内容进行清点。

sentences.en: And they quickly figure out that they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们很快发现自己搞错了。

sentences.en: It wasn't 50 people that were killed.
sentences.zh: 丧生的不是50人。

sentences.en: It was closer to 70.
sentences.zh: 接近70人。

sentences.en: They take that information pretty quickly to an Air Force lawyer named Dean Corsak.
sentences.zh: 他们非常迅速地将这一信息带给了一位名叫迪恩·科萨克的空军律师。

sentences.en: And his job in the operation center is basically to be the one there who knows the rules of law and can figure out what's a war crime and what isn't.
sentences.zh: 他在作战中心的工作基本上就是作为法律规则的知情者，判断什么是战争罪，什么不是。

sentences.en: And they flag it for him.
sentences.zh: 他们向他通报了这一情况。

sentences.en: And he immediately looks at the details and he decides,
sentences.zh: 他立即查看了细节并判定：

sentences.en: this is potentially a war crime.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一起战争罪。

sentences.en: And if it's a war crime, then regulations require that I report it.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一起战争罪，那么规章制度就要求我必须上报。

sentences.en: So Dave, why are they calling a lawyer here?
sentences.zh: 那么戴夫，他们为什么要在那里找律师？

sentences.en: What exactly about this strike is so unusual?
sentences.zh: 这次空袭究竟有什么不同寻常之处？

sentences.en: Well, I know that probably the public thinks of war as total chaos, but it's not total chaos.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道公众可能认为战争是一片彻底的混乱，但其实并非如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This war was fought overwhelmingly from the air.
sentences.zh: 这场战争绝大部分是从空中进行的。

sentences.en: And it was done that way in order to try and minimize the loss of life, both to civilians and to coalition troops.
sentences.zh: 之所以采用这种方式，是为了尽量减少平民和联军部队的生命损失。

sentences.en: And it relied overwhelmingly on a lot of drones with really good cameras that could study targets before they were hit to make
sentences.zh: 它在很大程度上依赖于大量配备极佳摄像头的无人机，这些无人机可以在打击目标之前对其进行研究，以确保

sentences.en: sure we're hitting the right place, the right people without civilians being in the way.
sentences.zh: 我们在打击正确地点、正确的人时不会殃及平民。

sentences.en: And to carry out this war with that level of precision, the military has reams of laws and regulations that control what they can target and who they can hit.
sentences.zh: 为了以这种精确度开展战争，军方制定了大量的法律和规章制度，来控制他们的打击目标和攻击对象。

sentences.en: There are levels of different people that are watching to make sure that the wrong call isn't made.
sentences.zh: 有不同层级的人员在进行监督，以确保不会做出错误的决定。

sentences.en: And if there is a mistake, if civilians are killed, there's a reporting process where people count the dead and make those figures public.
sentences.zh: 如果确实发生了错误，如果有平民被杀，就会有一个报告流程，由人们清点死者并将这些数字公之于众。

sentences.en: But what was interesting with this strike is that the Air Force lawyer, Dean Corsak, he didn't see any of those safeguards taking place.
sentences.zh: 但这次空袭有趣的地方在于，空军律师迪恩·科萨克并没有看到任何这些保障措施在起作用。

sentences.en: The footage that they were looking at didn't show any clear targets that would justify killing so many women and children.
sentences.zh: 他们观看的录像并未显示出任何足以证明杀死如此多妇女和儿童是正当的清晰目标。

sentences.en: And so to him, on a couple different levels, this seemed to violate those laws of armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 因此在他看来，在几个不同的层面上，这似乎都违反了武装冲突法。

sentences.en: So the first thing he does is he immediately preserves evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以他做的第一件事就是立即保存证据。

sentences.en: He calls into the squadron that oversees the fighter jets and has them preserve their video.
sentences.zh: 他打电话给监督战斗机的中队，让他们保存视频。

sentences.en: He preserves the logs of chats and strikes that oversaw this so that whoever's going to investigate it has what they need to figure out what happened.
sentences.zh: 他保存了监督此次行动的聊天记录和打击日志，以便将来无论是谁调查，都能拥有弄清真相所需的东西。

sentences.en: And then he does what he's supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 然后他做了他应该做的事。

sentences.en: He takes this report to his boss, the chief legal officer, who's an Air Force colonel.
sentences.zh: 他将这份报告呈报给他的上司——首席法律顾问，那是一位空军上校。

sentences.en: And that chief legal officer briefs his commander, who's a general.
sentences.zh: 这位首席法律顾问向他的指挥官（一位将军）做了简报。

sentences.en: But from there, it just sort of fizzles out.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，事情就不了了之了。

sentences.en: It doesn't get the required reporting to higher authorities that it's supposed to.
sentences.zh: 它没有按照规定上报给理应知情的更高层级主管。

sentences.en: And the lawyer doesn't really understand why.
sentences.zh: 这位律师实在无法理解原因。

sentences.en: And so eventually, he goes to the Air Force's version of the FBI, which is called the Office of
sentences.zh: 于是最终，他找到了空军版的FBI，也就是所谓的

sentences.en: Special Investigations.
sentences.zh: 特别调查办公室。

sentences.en: And he asks their agents, hey, is there something that you can do with this?
sentences.zh: 他问他们的特工：嘿，你们能对这件事做点什么吗？

sentences.en: Can you investigate this?
sentences.zh: 你们能调查一下吗？

sentences.en: And the response he gets is really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 而他得到的回复非常惊人。

sentences.en: We were able to get the email and I'll just read it.
sentences.zh: 我们拿到了这封电子邮件，我直接念一下。

sentences.en: When he asked them, you know, is this something you would look into?
sentences.zh: 当他问他们，你知道的，这事你们会介入调查吗？

sentences.en: They said, and I'm going to paraphrase here just for a second, not unless it's considered substantial.
sentences.zh: 他们回答说——我在这里稍微意译一下——除非被认为性质严重。

sentences.en: And then he goes on to say, examples include potentials for high media attention, concern with outcry from local government, and concern sensitive images may get out.
sentences.zh: 接着他又说：例子包括引起高度媒体关注的潜力、对地方政府强烈抗议的担忧，以及对敏感画面可能泄露的担忧。

sentences.en: So essentially, he's saying like, unless someone's going to catch us at this, it's not our job to look into it.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，他的意思是：除非有人会因此抓到我们的把柄，否则调查这事不归我们管。

sentences.en: So the group that's supposed to look into these things for the Air Force is just saying flat out, no.
sentences.zh: 因此，本该为空军调查这些事情的组织却直截了当地说：不。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the Air Force lawyer, Dean Corsak, starts to figure out that his chain of command likely isn't going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 所以空军律师迪恩·科萨克开始意识到，他的指挥链很可能不会采取任何行动。

sentences.en: And the criminal investigators don't seem they're going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 而刑事调查人员看起来也不会做任何事。

sentences.en: Maybe no one's going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 也许谁都不会采取行动。

sentences.en: And so he looks around and goes to what he sees as his last resort.
sentences.zh: 于是他四处张望，走向了他所认为的最后防线。

sentences.en: The independent watchdog for the military, the Department of Defense inspector general's office.
sentences.zh: 军方的独立监督机构，即国防部督察长办公室。

sentences.en: And he reaches out through a hotline they have and sends them a message saying, essentially, I think I witnessed a war crime.
sentences.zh: 他通过他们设立的热线联系了他们，发了一条消息，大意是：我认为我目睹了一起战争罪。

sentences.en: I believe that it's required that we investigate.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有责任展开调查。

sentences.en: I need your help.
sentences.zh: 我需要你们的帮助。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能查阅所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: So I want to go to the hotline.
sentences.zh: 所以我想联系热线。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Put me where you were when you were notified about it.
sentences.zh: 把我带回你收到相关通知时的场景。

sentences.en: So Dave, what happens once Dean's tip hits the hotline at the inspector general's office?
sentences.zh: 那么戴夫，一旦迪恩的线索传到督察长办公室的热线，会发生什么？

sentences.en: So I was notified of it by my immediate supervisor.
sentences.zh: 我收到了我的直接主管的通知。

sentences.en: It lands on the desk of an experienced government employee and former Navy officer named Eugene Tate.
sentences.zh: 它落在了尤金·泰特（Eugene Tate）的桌上，他是一位经验丰富的政府雇员兼前海军军官。

sentences.en: He came in to me and said, Gene, we received a hotline call that's related to your project.
sentences.zh: 他走到我面前说：吉恩，我们接到一个与你的项目相关的热线电话。

sentences.en: So we're going to take a look at it and see, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要去看一看，了解一下情况。

sentences.en: In a way, he was the perfect guy for this because not only did he have a lot of experience, but
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他是处理这件事的最佳人选，因为他不仅经验丰富，

sentences.en: he'd already been working on a report about civilian casualty reporting in Syria and Iraq when this tip arrived.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个线索到达时，他已经在撰写一份关于叙利亚和伊拉克平民伤亡报告的工作了。

sentences.en: And so when this tip lands on his desk...
sentences.zh: 因此，当这个线索落在他桌上时……

sentences.en: I immediately start to try to find information that will help me support his claim or to
sentences.zh: 我立即开始尝试寻找能帮我支持他的说法的证据，或者

sentences.en: see that it's bogus.
sentences.zh: 看出这是虚假举报。

sentences.en: He goes into the classified databases and he pulls up a lot of the video and other evidence that there is.
sentences.zh: 他登录机密数据库，提取了大量视频和其他证据。

sentences.en: And he starts to watch it.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始观看。

sentences.en: When I looked at the video, my first thought was, holy shit.
sentences.zh: 当我看到这段视频时，我的第一反应是：卧槽。

sentences.en: That was my first thought.
sentences.zh: 那是我的第一反应。

sentences.en: And what he sees is, you know, this large group of women and children
sentences.zh: 他看到的是，你知道的，这大群的妇女和儿童

sentences.en: huddled in a place where there doesn't seem to be a lot of action.
sentences.zh: 挤在一个似乎没有什么军事行动的地方。

sentences.en: Yes, I see people with weapons.
sentences.zh: 是的，我看到有人拿着武器。

sentences.en: Not a lot.
sentences.zh: 不多。

sentences.en: I see like two people with weapons.
sentences.zh: 我看到大约两个人拿着武器。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be much going on.
sentences.zh: 似乎没发生什么事。

sentences.en: And then suddenly...
sentences.zh: 然后突然……

sentences.en: Big boom.
sentences.zh: 一声巨响。

sentences.en: And I mean big boom.
sentences.zh: 我是说超级巨响。

sentences.en: He just describes this really big boom.
sentences.zh: 他这样描述这声巨大的轰鸣。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: That takes up the whole screen?
sentences.zh: 占据了整个屏幕？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And so he knows that he has to talk to the person who gave him this tip.
sentences.zh: 所以他知道他必须和那个提供线索的人谈谈。

sentences.en: So we went down and we interviewed him.
sentences.zh: 于是我们过去采访了他。

sentences.en: Their mission is basically to decide, is this guy credible?
sentences.zh: 他们的任务基本上是判断：这个人可信吗？

sentences.en: Because if it's a credible report, then regulations require that the military report and investigate it.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这是一份可信的报告，那么规章制度就要求军方进行报告和调查。

sentences.en: I think we did about a three or four-hour interview where we were just asking him questions about what he saw.
sentences.zh: 我想我们进行了大约三到四个小时的采访，我们只是向他询问有关他所见所闻的问题。

sentences.en: And he comes away thinking that this guy is...
sentences.zh: 最后他得出的结论是，这个人……

sentences.en: This guy is extremely credible.
sentences.zh: 这个人极具信誉。

sentences.en: Extremely credible.
sentences.zh: 极具信誉。

sentences.en: Everything he saw, his memory of the events, everything.
sentences.zh: 他所看到的一切，他对事件的记忆，一切都是如此。

sentences.en: And like I said, what he told us when we met with him was, I did this because I felt I had no other recourse.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，他跟我们见面时告诉我们：我这么做是因为我觉得自己别无选择。

sentences.en: I'd been talking to my chain of command.
sentences.zh: 我一直在跟我的指挥链沟通。

sentences.en: I've done all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我做了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And every place I go, they try to shut me down.
sentences.zh: 但我去到哪里，他们都试图把我压下去。

sentences.en: And very quickly, his team calls a meeting with their superiors at the inspector general's office and say, hey, this is potentially a war crime.
sentences.zh: 很快，他的团队与督察长办公室的上级召开了一次会议，并说：嘿，这可能是一起战争罪。

sentences.en: This is big.
sentences.zh: 这事很大。

sentences.en: We need to report it right away.
sentences.zh: 我们需要立即上报。

sentences.en: So how does he move forward?
sentences.zh: 那么他该如何继续推进行动呢？

sentences.en: Well, he tries to start gathering evidence to suss that out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他开始尝试搜集证据来弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: I immediately start using connections, and we obtained a copy of the CCAR, which is the civilian casualty assessment report.
sentences.zh: 我立刻开始利用人脉，我们搞到了一份 CCAR 的副本，也就是平民伤亡评估报告。

sentences.en: He gets his hands on some reports that look at the strike.
sentences.zh: 他弄到了一些关于这次空袭的报告。

sentences.en: When you read the actual narrative that was in the CCAR, it was, yeah, this doesn't make any sense at all type of stuff.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读 CCAR 里的实际叙述时，就会觉得，天哪，这简直毫无道理。

sentences.en: And immediately, he notices something odd.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，他注意到了一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: The number of confirmed casualty deaths doesn't match what he sees in the video.
sentences.zh: 确认的死亡人数与他在视频中看到的根本对不上。

sentences.en: In fact, it's just a tiny fraction.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这只是极小的一部分。

sentences.en: And he can't figure out where the military is getting its numbers from.
sentences.zh: 而且他搞不懂军方的数字是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: As an intel guy, when you're reading something, you always want to know what's the source and how did they come up with this conclusion.
sentences.zh: 作为一个情报人员，当你阅读材料时，你总是想知道信息来源是什么，他们是怎么得出这个结论的。

sentences.en: And they would say things in the narrative that I'm like, well, how did they get there?
sentences.zh: 报告里有些叙述让我不禁想：他们是怎么得出这种说法的？

sentences.en: You know, because it wasn't sourced.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为它根本没有注明出处。

sentences.en: It wasn't per this or according to this or whatever.
sentences.zh: 上面没有写“根据这个”或“依据那个”之类的话。

sentences.en: It was just like, it was stated as a fact.
sentences.zh: 它就好像是被当成既定事实直接写出来的。

sentences.en: And then on the last page of the report, there was something else that really didn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 然后，在报告的最后一页，还有一些东西实在让人匪夷所思。

sentences.en: There was a section that was reserved for the opinions of the operations officer and the legal officer, the military lawyer.
sentences.zh: 有一个章节是专门留给作战军官和法律军官（也就是军方律师）的意见的。

sentences.en: I can't remember the way it is exactly worded, but it was basically they expressed that they had concerns with the, in this case, they called it the law of armed conflict.
sentences.zh: 我记不清具体是怎么措辞的了，但大意是他们表达了对——在这个案例中，他们称之为武装冲突法——的担忧。

sentences.en: And there he found that both officers wrote, they thought that a law of armed conflict violation, a war crime may have happened.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他发现两位军官都写道，他们认为可能发生了一起违反武装冲突法的事件，也就是战争罪。

sentences.en: But then something strange happened.
sentences.zh: 但随后，诡异的事情发生了。

sentences.en: He got another copy of the report, this time one that had been given to him by the command of the special operations group.
sentences.zh: 他拿到了这份报告的另一份副本，这一次是特种作战部队司令部交给他的。

sentences.en: And that report left all of those comments out on the back page.
sentences.zh: 那份报告把最后一页的所有评论全都删掉了。

sentences.en: It's not that it was redacted.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说被涂黑了。

sentences.en: It's that it's as if nothing had ever been written there.
sentences.zh: 而是那种感觉，就好像那里从来没有写过任何东西一样。

sentences.en: And he didn't know what to do with that.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该拿这怎么办。

sentences.en: It seemed to him like someone was trying to cover something up.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，这就像是有人在试图掩盖什么。

sentences.en: And so what does he do with all this contradictory information?
sentences.zh: 那么，面对所有这些矛盾的信息，他该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Honestly, he doesn't know what to do because he's an experienced evaluator, but he's not a criminal investigator.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他根本不知道该怎么办，因为他是个经验丰富的评估员，但不是刑事调查员。

sentences.en: He doesn't have the power to sort of dig into this and really get answers.
sentences.zh: 他没有权力去深入挖掘并真正得到答案。

sentences.en: And so he feels like what he has to do, what everyone at his organization has to do is just report it so that the top folks in the military can get to the bottom of it.
sentences.zh: 因此他觉得，他必须要做的事，也就是他所在组织里每个人必须要做的事，就是向上级汇报，以便军方高层能查明真相。

sentences.en: And we had a meeting where you literally go in with all the big, big wigs.
sentences.zh: 我们开过一个会，你简直是直接去和所有的大人物当面对质。

sentences.en: And his team takes this information to their superiors.
sentences.zh: 他的团队把这些信息带给了他们的上级。

sentences.en: And we, we lay out everything.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们把一切都摆在了桌面上。

sentences.en: We explain to them that we've seen video.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们解释说我们看过视频。

sentences.en: We explain to them all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们解释了所有这些情况。

sentences.en: We think it's very serious.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这非常严重。

sentences.en: And they basically all just nod their heads and go.
sentences.zh: 而他们基本上都只是点点头，然后就过去了。

sentences.en: They don't really come to a decision.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有真正做出决定。

sentences.en: So there's no action.
sentences.zh: 所以没有任何行动。

sentences.en: No action.
sentences.zh: 没有任何行动。

sentences.en: So they draw up a memo that would do all of the work of notifying this.
sentences.zh: 于是他们起草了一份备忘录，用来完成通知上级的这项工作。

sentences.en: And all their superior, the man who oversees their section, has to do is sign the memo and the notification will go forward.
sentences.zh: 他们上级（也就是负责他们那个部门的人）所需要做的，只是在备忘录上签个字，通知就能发出去了。

sentences.en: And that memo goes unsigned.
sentences.zh: 但那份备忘录始终没有签字。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But he decides he has one more option.
sentences.zh: 但他决定自己还有最后一个选择。

sentences.en: He's already working on that report that's broadly looking at problems with civilian casualties in Iraq and Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他已经在着手编写那份关于伊拉克和阿富汗平民伤亡普遍问题的报告。

sentences.en: And he figures, OK, if no one will report it, we can put it into this report.
sentences.zh: 他盘算着，好吧，既然没人愿意报告，那我们就把它写进这份报告里。

sentences.en: Because this report is going to go to Congress and it's going to go to top leaders at the Pentagon and they'll see it.
sentences.zh: 因为这份报告将会呈交给国会，也会呈交给五角大楼的高层领导，他们会看到的。

sentences.en: But that project took over two years to complete.
sentences.zh: 但那个项目花了两两年多的时间才完成。

sentences.en: For reasons that he can't really get a clear answer on, the report gets slowed, delayed.
sentences.zh: 由于种种他无法得到明确解释的原因，这份报告被拖延了。

sentences.en: The report was written and rewritten and re-edited and edited numerous times by the leadership.
sentences.zh: 这份报告被领导层反复撰写、重写、重新编辑修改了无数次。

sentences.en: And there was some belief that it was trying to, how do I say this, downplay some of the issues that had occurred.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种看法认为，他们是在试图，我该怎么说呢，淡化所发生的一些问题。

sentences.en: I'll say it that way.
sentences.zh: 我只能这么说了。

sentences.en: And in the end, there's no mention of this strike anywhere in the report.
sentences.zh: 最终，报告的任何地方都没有提及这次空袭。

sentences.en: It seems like if he was suspicious that this was a cover-up before, he's probably feeling pretty sure that it's a cover-up now.
sentences.zh: 如果说他之前还只是怀疑这是一场掩盖行动，那他现在大概可以百分之百确信这就是一场掩盖了。

sentences.en: I don't know if he'd go that far, but he was definitely confused.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他会不会下这么绝对的结论，但他确实感到很困惑。

sentences.en: Things that he was trying to find answers to just weren't adding up.
sentences.zh: 他一直在试图寻找答案的事情根本对不上号。

sentences.en: And he kept going to people, telling them that this needed to be reported.
sentences.zh: 他不断地去找其他人，告诉他们这件事必须上报。

sentences.en: And he thought it was a pretty simple request to just do what the regulations say.
sentences.zh: 他原本以为这只是个非常简单的要求，也就是按规章制度办事。

sentences.en: But he kept running into, you know, roadblocks, getting the runaround, all sorts of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但他不断碰到各种绊脚石，被踢皮球，遇到各种各样的事。

sentences.en: And he did feel that by the end, no one wanted to hear what he had to say.
sentences.zh: 到最后他确实感觉到，根本没有人愿意听他说话。

sentences.en: There was one point where he said to me, man, I wish there was an inspector general for the inspector generals.
sentences.zh: 有一次他对我说，老天，我希望总监察长上面还能有个总监察长。

sentences.en: You know, and so what happened to him eventually is he just grew kind of angry about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以他最终的遭遇就是，对此感到有些愤怒。

sentences.en: And very vocally so.
sentences.zh: 而且表现得非常直言不讳。

sentences.en: He criticized the decisions to take this stuff out.
sentences.zh: 他批评了抹去这些材料的决定。

sentences.en: And one day he was called into his supervisor's office and told that his contract wasn't being renewed.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他被叫进了主管的办公室，被告知他的合同不会续签了。

sentences.en: And very quickly after that, he was escorted out of the building by security.
sentences.zh: 紧接着没过多久，他就被安保人员护送着离开了大楼。

sentences.en: And does he think it has to do with him trying to push people to look into this?
sentences.zh: 他认为这跟自己试图催促大家调查此事有关吗？

sentences.en: Of course, no one said it this way.
sentences.zh: 当然，没人会这么明说。

sentences.en: But he feels that it's directly related to this airstrike case where he kept trying to get the office to do something and was unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得这直接与那起空袭事件有关，当时他一直试图让办公室采取行动却屡屡碰壁。

sentences.en: So it sounds like he's just at a dead end.
sentences.zh: 听起来他似乎走投无路了。

sentences.en: Well, not quite.
sentences.zh: 嗯，倒也未必。

sentences.en: He figures he's got one move left.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己还有最后一招。

sentences.en: He goes to Congress.
sentences.zh: 他去找了国会。

sentences.en: And he sets up a meeting with the Senate Armed Services Committee staff.
sentences.zh: 他跟参议院军事委员会的工作人员安排了一场会面。

sentences.en: And he provides them with several pages of documentation, you know, not giving away any classified information, but telling them where they can get it and everything that happened.
sentences.zh: 他向他们提供了好几页的文档，当然，没有泄露任何机密信息，但告诉了他们去哪里获取这些信息以及发生的一切。

sentences.en: And they say they'll look into it.
sentences.zh: 他们表示会调查此事。

sentences.en: And he feels like he's finally reached the right authorities and something's going to get done.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己终于找到了对的权力机构，事情总算要有着落了。

sentences.en: And so he waits and he waits and he waits and three or four months go by and nothing's happening.
sentences.zh: 于是他等啊等，等啊等，三四个月过去了，却什么动静也没有。

sentences.en: And that's when, out of the blue, I get a call from him.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我突然接到了他打来的电话。

sentences.en: And the reason that he's calling me is I already knew about this strike.
sentences.zh: 他之所以打电话给我，是因为我之前就已经知道了这次空袭。

sentences.en: And I'd learned from other sources that it had been ordered by a classified special operations unit on the ground.
sentences.zh: 我从其他渠道了解到，这是由地面上一支机密的特种作战部队下令发动的。

sentences.en: And for months, I had been going around, emailing and calling anyone I could find, trying to piece this story together.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，我一直在到处奔走，给所有能找到的人发邮件、打电话，试图把这个故事拼凑起来。

sentences.en: And Eugene was this guy who I knew I had to get in touch with because he not only had studied it in detail, but he had written a report about it.
sentences.zh: 而尤金就是我早就知道必须联系的人，因为他不仅对此进行了深入研究，还写过一份相关报告。

sentences.en: And so I emailed him, I called him.
sentences.zh: 于是我给他发邮件、打电话。

sentences.en: I never heard back for months.
sentences.zh: 好几个月我都没得到任何回复。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, here he is on the phone and he's willing to talk.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，他打来电话，并且愿意开口了。

sentences.en: I mean, he was very clear he'd tell me what he knew, but that he wasn't going to divulge any classified information or leak any classified materials because, of course,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常明确地表示会告诉我他所知道的情况，但他不会泄露任何机密信息或机密材料，因为当然了，

sentences.en: that's illegal.
sentences.zh: 那是违法的。

sentences.en: And it was interesting because there were a lot of things he couldn't tell me.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，有很多事情他确实无法告诉我。

sentences.en: You know, he couldn't even tell us even the name of the special operations group at the center of this because it's all classified.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他甚至不能告诉我们处于风口浪尖的那支特种作战部队的名字，因为这全都是机密。

sentences.en: But my colleague, Eric Schmidt, and I were able to piece it together and we figured out that the unit behind all of this was a secretive unit called Task Force 9.
sentences.zh: 但我的同事埃里克·施密特和我最终把线索拼凑在了一起，我们发现幕后的那支部队是一支名为“第九特遣队”的神秘部队。

sentences.en: And who is Task Force 9?
sentences.zh: 那第九特遣队到底是谁？

sentences.en: That's kind of hard to say because so much of what they do is top secret.
sentences.zh: 这很难说清楚，因为他们的许多行动都属于绝密。

sentences.en: But, you know, basically, they're a special operations force.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，基本上他们就是一支特种作战部队。

sentences.en: We're pretty confident they're mostly made up of Army Delta Force commandos and Special Forces Green Berets.
sentences.zh: 我们相当确信，他们主要由美国陆军三角洲部队突击队员和特种部队绿色贝雷帽组成。

sentences.en: And their job was to basically be the ground troops that worked with local militias who are fighting the Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 他们的职责基本上就是充当与打击伊斯兰国的当地民兵并肩作战的地面部队。

sentences.en: And most critically,
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，

sentences.en: their job was to call in the airstrikes from the coalition because the coalition had this massive amount of air power that could have turned the whole ISIS caliphate into duSt.
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是呼叫联军的空袭，因为联军拥有庞大的空中火力，本可以把整个 ISIS 哈里发国化为灰烬。

sentences.en: But they needed someone to take that power and essentially direct it.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要有人来掌控这股力量并进行实质性的指挥。

sentences.en: And that's what the group did.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个小组所做的事。

sentences.en: But, you know, we don't know much more about them than that because everything they do is classified.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于他们我们也就知道这么多了，因为他们所做的一切都是机密。

sentences.en: We were only able to patch together little parts of it.
sentences.zh: 我们只能东拼西凑地了解一些边角料。

sentences.en: And one of them was a really intriguing report, top secret report that went through the inspector general's office.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是一份非常引人入胜的绝密报告，这份报告经由监察长办公室流出。

sentences.en: Eugene Tate refused to talk to me about it because it was so top secret, but we figured out parts of it on our own.
sentences.zh: 尤金·泰特拒绝和我谈论此事，因为它实在是绝密，但我们自己弄懂了一些部分。

sentences.en: And in that report, the CIA had seen what Task Force 9 was doing and they were upset about it.
sentences.zh: 在那份报告中，中情局注意到了第九特遣队的所作所为，并对此感到非常不满。

sentences.en: And they went to the inspector general and said essentially, hey, in several airstrikes, this task force is killing a number of civilians and possibly breaking the law.
sentences.zh: 他们找到监察长，大意是说：嘿，在好几起空袭中，这支特遣队杀害了许多平民，可能已经触犯了法律。

sentences.en: And then we were able to figure out that the Air Force and other staff that were in the command center, they were seeing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 接着我们了解到，指挥中心里的空军和其他工作人员也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: They were seeing all sorts of strikes that seemed to be hitting targets where there may have been enemies, but civilians were getting hit too.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了形形色色的空袭，这些空袭打击的目标似乎确实可能有敌人，但也连累了平民。

sentences.en: And they started to notice something really odd that repeatedly in strike after strike, they were calling them in saying that these were self-defense strikes.
sentences.zh: 他们开始注意到一件非常诡异的事，在一次又一次的空袭中，他们反复呼叫支援，并声称这些都是自卫空袭。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, self-defense, there are rules for when you can hit a target.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所谓自卫，对于何时可以打击目标是有规章制度的。

sentences.en: And a lot of times the people that decide whether those rules are being followed are in some command center somewhere and they're going to go through it and they're going to give you a thumbs up or a thumbs down.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，决定这些规则是否得到遵守的人身处某处的指挥中心，他们会进行审核，然后给出批准或否决。

sentences.en: But there is a way that you can skip all of that oversight very quickly by saying that you're under imminent threat and you need to defend yourself.
sentences.zh: 但有一种方法可以迅速绕过所有这些监督，那就是声称你正面临迫在眉睫的威胁，需要进行自卫。

sentences.en: Under the law of war, that is always allowed.
sentences.zh: 根据战争法，这是永远被允许的。

sentences.en: And that allowed the task force to skip all of the officers, all of the oversight,
sentences.zh: 这使得特遣队能够绕过所有的军官、所有的监督、

sentences.en: all of the lawyers that had rule books and talk directly to the aircraft that were going to hit their target.
sentences.zh: 所有那些手握规则手册的律师，直接与即将打击目标的战机进行通话。

sentences.en: And so they could hit what they wanted to essentially with no one second guessing them.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们基本上可以随心所欲地打击目标，而没有人会去质疑他们。

sentences.en: Sort of short circuiting directly to the airplane and skipping the lawyers and all of the steps they were supposed to go through for protection.
sentences.zh: 这就好比直接短路连通了飞机，跳过了律师以及他们为了保护平民本该经历的所有步骤。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, it won't surprise you that no one in the military thinks that you shouldn't be able to do that when you need to.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当你有需要时理应可以这样做，军方没有任何人会对此感到意外。

sentences.en: But what people in the operation center started seeing was that Task Force 9 seemed to be using this justification almost all of the time.
sentences.zh: 但作战中心的人开始发现的是，第九特遣队似乎几乎在所有时候都在使用这个正当理由。

sentences.en: Technically, they were supposed to be behind enemy lines.
sentences.zh: 按技术规定，他们本该深入敌后。

sentences.en: They're not in the fight.
sentences.zh: 他们并不在前线作战。

sentences.en: And yet what we were told is that sometimes 80 percent of their strikes were being justified as, you know, we're under imminent harm.
sentences.zh: 然而我们得到的消息却是，有时他们 80% 的空袭都以“我们正遭受迫在眉睫的伤害”为由进行辩解。

sentences.en: We need to call in self-defense.
sentences.zh: 我们需要呼叫自卫支援。

sentences.en: So it's essentially this was supposed to be an extreme measure, but it had become a habit that they were relying on.
sentences.zh: 所以这本来应该是一种极端手段，但却成了他们习惯性依赖的借口。

sentences.en: It had become the status quo.
sentences.zh: 这已经成了常态。

sentences.en: And the people in the operation center would go back and sometimes review these strikes and look for evidence of self-defense.
sentences.zh: 作战中心的人会回过头来，有时会审查这些空袭并寻找自卫的证据。

sentences.en: And they would never see or at least rarely see anything that showed that troops were under fire.
sentences.zh: 但他们从来没有（或者说极少）看到任何能证明部队当时正遭受炮火攻击的迹象。

sentences.en: And in the case of this strike that we've been talking about, four days after it was, you know, marked down as self-defense,
sentences.zh: 而在我们一直在谈论的这次空袭中，在它被记为自卫性质的四天之后，

sentences.en: satellite imagery shows that coalition forces came in with a bulldozer and literally buried the evidence.
sentences.zh: 卫星图像显示，联军部队开着推土机来到现场，直接把证据给埋了。

sentences.en: You know, in a real way, the deaths of women and children were covered up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，妇女和儿童的死亡就这样实实在在地被掩盖了。

sentences.en: So now there's really no way to get a precise count.
sentences.zh: 所以现在根本无法获得精确的统计数字。

sentences.en: The evidence is actually buried.
sentences.zh: 证据实际上已经被埋掉了。

sentences.en: I mean, the American military tried to make this the most precise and accountable air war in its history and report everything publicly and investigate every single casualty.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美军曾试图将其打造为其历史上最精准、最透明的空战，将一切公之于众，并调查每一起伤亡。

sentences.en: And it held that up to show that it was being transparent and accountable.
sentences.zh: 他们以此来标榜自己的透明和负责。

sentences.en: But in fact, a lot of those processes were used to do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，其中许多流程却被用来达到相反的目的。

sentences.en: You know, you could hold up a report that said that nothing happened, even though it was totally clear, even to the military, that something had.
sentences.zh: 你可以拿着一份声称什么都没发生的报告大肆宣扬，尽管哪怕对军方而言，事情明明已经发生得一清二楚。

sentences.en: And the thing is, like, all of this stuff is classified.
sentences.zh: 问题是，所有这些东西都是机密的。

sentences.en: We don't really get to see any of it.
sentences.zh: 我们根本看不到任何内容。

sentences.en: We don't know the scope.
sentences.zh: 我们无从得知其规模有多大。

sentences.en: One of the few glimpses that we get into it is this one airstrike that all these guys were trying to report.
sentences.zh: 我们能窥见冰山一角的少数机会之一，就是这起所有人都在试图上报的空袭。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what I'm taking away from this story, then, is that there really isn't any accountability when it comes to airstrikes in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个故事中我得到的结论是，美国军方在空袭这件事上根本没有任何问责制可言。

sentences.en: military.
sentences.zh: 军方。,军方。 (此处重复对应语境)

sentences.en: Well, I think that there are people in the military that really want there to be accountability and have worked hard to try and ensure that there's accountability.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为军中确实有人真心希望实现问责，并且一直在努力确保问责制的落实。

sentences.en: But the system that they've created is still so flawed that it doesn't really tell us anything meaningful about, you know, how many civilians were actually killed.
sentences.zh: 但他们建立的体制依然存在如此严重的漏洞，以至于它根本无法向我们提供任何有意义的信息，让我们知道到底有多少平民遇害。

sentences.en: I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想想看。

sentences.en: Here was a case where 70 people were killed, and they were killed in front of a high-definition colored drone camera that lots of military people saw.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有 70 人丧生的案例，而且他们是在许多军人都能看到的、高清彩色无人机摄像头的眼皮底下被杀害的。

sentences.en: It was immediately reported, and then it was reported again and again, and the system was unable to respond in any logical way.
sentences.zh: 事情立刻就被上报了，然后又一次次被上报，然而整个体制却无法做出任何合乎逻辑的反应。

sentences.en: I mean, if the system can't handle something as obvious as that, what can it handle?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果系统连这么明显的问题都处理不了，那它还能处理什么？

sentences.en: Dave, thank you.
sentences.zh: 戴夫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: After the New York Times sent its findings to U.S.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》将其调查结果发送给美国

sentences.en: Central Command, which oversaw the air war in Syria, the command acknowledged the strikes for the first time.
sentences.zh: 中央司令部（该司令部负责监督叙利亚的空战）后，该司令部首次承认了这些空袭。

sentences.en: In a statement, they said the strikes were justified and that 80 people were killed, including 16 fighters and four civilians.
sentences.zh: 他们在声明中表示，空袭是正当的，共有80人被杀，其中包括16名战斗人员和4名平民。

sentences.en: As for the other 60 dead, the statement said it was not clear that they were civilians, in part because women and children in the Islamic State sometimes took up arMs.
sentences.zh: 至于其余60名死者，声明称尚不清楚他们是否为平民，部分原因是伊斯兰国的妇女和儿童有时会拿起武器。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: I propose that the revised proposal is adopted as orally amended.
sentences.zh: 我提议采纳经口头修正后的修订提案。

sentences.en: A revised version, a written version, will be issued shortly.
sentences.zh: 修订版，即书面版本，将于近期发布。

sentences.en: Hearing no objections, it is so decided.
sentences.zh: 如果没有异议，那就这样决定了。

sentences.en: On Saturday, at the U.N.
sentences.zh: 周六，在联合国

sentences.en: Climate Conference in Glasgow, negotiators from nearly 200 countries struck a deal designed to speed up efforts to fight climate change.
sentences.zh: 格拉斯哥气候大会上，来自近200个国家的谈判代表达成了一项旨在加速应对气候变化努力的协议。

sentences.en: But the agreement failed to reach the breakthrough needed to keep the Earth from heating more than 1.5 degrees Celsius,
sentences.zh: 但该协议未能达成防止地球升温超过1.5摄氏度所需的突破，

sentences.en: a critical threshold past which scientists warn the dangers to the climate grow dramatically.
sentences.zh: 科学家警告称，超过这个临界阈值，气候灾难将会急剧加剧。

sentences.en: In the final hours of talks, negotiators watered down their wording on fossil fuels, calling on countries to phase down the use of coal instead of phase out.
sentences.zh: 在谈判的最后几个小时里，谈判代表淡化了关于化石燃料的措辞，呼吁各国“逐步减少”而非“逐步淘汰”煤炭的使用。

sentences.en: I have an intervention from Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 我收到了一条来自瑞士的发言请求。

sentences.en: Switzerland, I give you the floor.
sentences.zh: 瑞士，请发言。

sentences.en: On behalf of the EIG, we would like to express our profound disappointment that the language that we have agreed on, on coal and fossil fuel subordinates,
sentences.zh: 代表环境诚信集团（EIG），我们对我们已经达成的关于煤炭和化石燃料补贴的措辞

sentences.en: has been further watered down as a result of an intransparent process.
sentences.zh: 由于一个不透明的过程而被进一步淡化，表示深切的失望。

sentences.en: Leaders rose to object to the last-minute change.
sentences.zh: 领导人们纷纷起立反对这最后一刻的更改。

sentences.en: And island nations said the agreement fell far short of what they need.
sentences.zh: 岛国则表示，该协议远远没有达到他们的需求。

sentences.en: It will be too late for the Maldives.
sentences.zh: 对于马尔代夫来说，那就太晚了。

sentences.en: I would like to remind us all that we have 98 months to halve global emissions.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒大家，我们只有98个月的时间将全球排放量减半。

sentences.en: The difference between 1.5 and 2 degrees is a death sentence for us.
sentences.zh: 1.5度与2度之间的差距对我们来说就是死刑判决。

sentences.en: And on Friday,
sentences.zh: 而在周五，

sentences.en: a judge in Los Angeles released pop star Britney Spears from a restrictive legal arrangement called a conservatorship that had stripped the singer of control over almost every aspect of her life for nearly 14 years.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶的一名法官解除了流行歌星布兰妮·斯皮尔斯的限制性法律安排（即监护权），该安排剥夺了这位歌手近14年来对其生活几乎所有方面的控制权。

sentences.en: This is a monumental day for Britney Spears.
sentences.zh: 这对布兰妮·斯皮尔斯来说具有划时代的意义。

sentences.en: Speaking outside the court, her lawyer said the agreement was terminated immediately and that her case had shined a light on abuses in the wider system.
sentences.zh: 她的律师在法院外发言时表示，该协议已立即终止，她的案件揭露了更广泛系统中的虐待行为。

sentences.en: As a result of Britney, Congress has heard her at the federal level.
sentences.zh: 由于布兰妮的原因，国会在联邦层面听取了她的诉求。

sentences.en: The United States Senate and the United States House of Representatives are looking at this conservatorship and conservatorships generally with an eye toward passing legislation to ensure that people are not abused.
sentences.zh: 美国参议院和美国众议院正在审视这项监护权以及普遍的监护权制度，旨在通过立法以确保人们免受虐待。

sentences.en: If this happens to Britney, it can happen to anybody.
sentences.zh: 如果这发生在她身上，它就可以发生在任何人身上。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderplug, Daniel Guimet, and Claire Tennis-Sketter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普鲁格、丹尼尔·吉梅特和克莱尔·坦尼斯-斯凯特制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Larissa Anderson and Michael Benoit and features original music by Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 由拉里萨·安德森和迈克尔·博努瓦剪辑，原创音乐由马里昂·洛扎诺创作。

sentences.en: It was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德进行音频工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Landsverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布朗伯格和本·兰兹维克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尔尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何平台上收听。
